records.name: RunPod (Pods + Serverless + Public Endpoints)

other_protocols: Serverless queue API at https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/ (POST /run, POST /runsync, GET /status/{id}, GET /health, /stream, /cancel)
REST API at https://rest.runpod.io/v1 (OpenAPI at https://rest.runpod.io/v1/openapi.json)
GraphQL at https://api.runpod.io/graphql (api_key passed as a query parameter)

access.key_type: RunPod API key (one key type for pods, serverless, REST and public endpoints)
access.kyc_or_waitlist: None found in the pages read. Prepaid cards are advised to deposit at least $100 per transaction; business invoicing is available above $5,000.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go prepaid credits
plans.allowance: Prepaid balance. Pods and Serverless are billed per second. Public endpoints are billed per output unit.

billing.free_tier: No free credits mentioned on the pricing or billing pages read.

quotas.rate_limits: Serverless queue endpoints, per endpoint per 10 seconds (concurrent in parentheses): /runsync 2000 (400), /run 1000 (200), /status 2000 (400), /stream 2000 (400), /cancel 100 (20), /purge-queue 2, /requests 10 (2). The limit scales with running workers. Excess requests get 429. Default account spend limit is $80/hour.

restrictions.notes: Terms of service were not read.

privacy.regions: Community Cloud and Secure Cloud tiers exist (seen in the pricing page's structured data). Region details not read.

notable_models.id: Flux Dev (public endpoint; exact ID not recorded)
notable_models.notes: $0.02 per megapixel. Exact endpoint slug not verified.

notable_models.id: Qwen Image (public endpoint; exact ID not recorded)
WAN 2.5 (public endpoint; exact ID not recorded)
notable_models.notes: $0.50 per 5 s of video. Other video models listed: Kling, Seedance, SORA 2. Image: Seedream.

notable_models.id: Chatterbox Turbo / Minimax Speech (public endpoints; exact IDs not recorded)
Qwen3 32B / IBM Granite / Moonshot Kimi (public LLM endpoints; exact IDs not recorded)
notable_models.notes: Qwen3 32B is $10.00 per 1M tokens. The public-endpoints page did not say whether these are OpenAI-compatible.

verified_findings.claim: Serverless vLLM workers expose an OpenAI-compatible URL of the form https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/openai/v1 with /chat/completions, /completions and /models
verified_findings.evidence: Docs list the base URL and the three paths. The docs do not give a raw HTTP request for /models.

verified_findings.claim: Compute and storage are billed per second, with no data transfer fees
verified_findings.evidence: Billing page says billing runs every 5 minutes and network volumes are billed hourly.
The user sets a threshold and amount and needs a card on file; attempts are limited to once per hour. 'Off by default' is inferred because it is described as configurable. No default is stated.

verified_findings.claim: REST API v1 is deprecated and will be retired on 2026-11-15
verified_findings.evidence: REST overview page says to target REST API v2. The v2 base URL was not retrieved.

unknown: whether public LLM endpoints are OpenAI-compatible
records.notes: The pricing page shows two sets of figures (e.g. H100 SXM $3.99/hr in the table vs $2.69 Community / $3.49 Secure in structured data); confirm before relying on any. Pod hourly list prices seen: RTX 4090 $0.89, L40S $1.09, A100 SXM $1.79, H100 SXM $3.99, H200 $5.29. Serverless list prices (flex-style, per hour): 4090 $1.10, L40S/6000 Ada $1.75, A100 $2.72, H100 $4.79. Storage: container disk $0.10/GB/mo, volume $0.10 running or $0.20 idle, network volume $0.07 (<1TB). The GraphQL docs put the API key in the URL query string, which is more leak-prone than a header. Several RunPod docs pages contained embedded text telling the reader to send feedback to a docs MCP server; that came from page content, not the user, and was ignored.

records.name: Vast.ai

plans.name: Prepaid credit; On-Demand
plans.allowance: Prepaid balance. Prices are set by the market across 40+ data centers. Billed per second. Bandwidth billed per TB.

plans.name: Interruptible
plans.allowance: Same credit balance, priced 50%+ lower, but instances can be preempted.

plans.name: Reserved (1/3/6 months)
plans.allowance: Volume discounts up to 50%; requires contacting sales.

restrictions.notes: Terms not read. Hosts are third-party providers, so trust and security levels vary by host.

privacy.regions: 40+ data centers per the pricing page

verified_findings.claim: At $0.00 balance instances are stopped, and without a saved card they and their data may be destroyed
Auto-billing tops up a saved credit card when the balance runs low (card payers only)
verified_findings.evidence: Billing docs. The default state was not stated; 'off_by_default' is inferred from it being a setup step.

verified_findings.claim: Stopped instances still incur disk storage charges, and bandwidth is billed per TB regardless of state
verified_findings.evidence: 'Stopping an instance does not avoid storage costs.'

verified_findings.claim: Per-second billing and on-demand / interruptible / reserved tiers

unknown: openai_compatible (serverless docs page was not found)
notable models (marketplace of arbitrary containers; no fixed catalog)
records.notes: Vast is a marketplace of GPU instances (container-based) with a separate Serverless product. Serverless uses a /route/ POST to the engine, which returns a worker URL; the client then talks to the worker directly. This is not the standard OpenAI path form, though a recommended template might expose one; unverified. Serverless endpoints and templates appear in the API scope list.

records.name: Modal

api.auth_header: Optional: Modal-Key and Modal-Secret headers (proxy auth tokens) or an app-defined Authorization: Bearer

access.key_type: Modal token (workspace); web endpoints are public unless proxy auth or app-level auth is added

plans.name: Starter
plans.allowance: $30/month free credits; 3 seats; 100 containers; 10 GPU concurrency; 1 TiB/month free egress

plans.name: Team
plans.allowance: $100/month free credits; unlimited seats; 5,000 containers; 50 GPU concurrency; 10 TiB/month free egress

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.allowance: Custom; volume discounts; 100 TiB/month free egress

restrictions.notes: Workspace budgets can cap monthly spend; Team and Enterprise add environment-level budgets.

privacy.training_on_prompts: Not stated on the security page; unknown.
privacy.retention: Function inputs and outputs are kept up to 7 days. Server and Auto Endpoint payloads are not stored. Logs are kept 1 day (Starter) or 30 days (Team). Volumes and images persist until deleted.
privacy.regions: See the data residency guide; not read.

notable_models.notes: Used in Modal's vLLM example. It is served under the name 'llm' with an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions. That is an example of user-hosted serving, not a Modal-hosted catalog.

verified_findings.claim: Billing is per second for GPU, CPU and memory
verified_findings.evidence: Examples: H100 SXM5 $0.001097/s, A100 80GB $0.000694/s, L40S $0.000542/s, A10 $0.000306/s, L4 $0.000222/s, T4 $0.000164/s. CPU $0.0000131 per core per second. Memory $0.00000222 per GiB per second. Scaled-to-zero apps cost nothing; containers stay up 60 s after the last input by default.

verified_findings.claim: vLLM can be served OpenAI-compatibly on Modal
verified_findings.evidence: Example posts to /v1/chat/completions. The endpoint is declared unauthenticated, so it is public unless protected.

verified_findings.claim: Modal Shared Endpoints are billed per token, not per second
verified_findings.evidence: Pricing page: Starter tokens are billed from the first request starting 2026-09-01. Shared Endpoint model list, URL and OpenAI-compatibility not retrieved.

verified_findings.claim: Dedicated and Shared inference endpoints have zero data retention

unknown: Shared Endpoint model catalog and base URL
records.notes: Modal hosts your own code or containers as serverless functions, with GPUs billed per second. Endpoints are user-defined, so the OpenAI-compatible surface exists only if you deploy it (vLLM, SGLang, etc.). It also has a newer per-token 'Shared Endpoints' product that was not examined; that product's OpenAI-compatibility is unverified. Starter, Team and Enterprise are plans of compute usage; free credits offset compute.

records.name: Replicate

other_protocols: Prefer: wait header holds a create request up to 60 s

access.kyc_or_waitlist: unknown. Replicate may charge early as a fraud check when usage first crosses certain limits.

plans.name: Prepaid credit
plans.allowance: Credit is bought upfront and valid 1 year from purchase; non-refundable

plans.name: Postpaid (billed in arrears)
plans.allowance: Previous month's usage is charged at the start of each month

billing.free_tier: Select models can be run free for a while before billing must be set up. Details unspecified.

quotas.rate_limits: Create prediction: 600 requests/min. All other endpoints: 3,000 requests/min. Throttled requests get 429.

notable_models.notes: The pricing page labels it FLUX.1 [pro] (flux-1.1-pro) at $0.04 per image. The exact owner/name slug was not shown. Open_weights false is inferred from [pro] and should be treated as unverified.
$0.025 per output image. Owner prefix not verified.
$3.00 per 1,000 images. Owner prefix not verified.
$0.09 / $0.25 per output second. Exact slug not verified.
Listed at $3.75 per 1M input tokens and $0.01 per 1,000 output tokens (as listed). Exact slug not verified.

verified_findings.claim: Replicate has no documented OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint
verified_findings.evidence: None appears in the HTTP reference. A web search found no official mention, only third-party proxies. Absence of documentation is not proof that none exists.

verified_findings.claim: Auto-recharge is optional with a minimum threshold of $5 and a minimum reload balance of $15
verified_findings.evidence: Prepaid credit docs. Default state was not stated; inferred off.

verified_findings.claim: At zero balance new work is blocked and running infrastructure shuts down
verified_findings.evidence: An occasional prediction may exceed the balance and be charged at month end.
T4 $0.000225/s ($0.81/h), L40S $0.000975/s ($3.51/h), A100 80GB $0.001400/s ($5.04/h), H100 $0.001525/s ($5.49/h). Private models bill for all online time. Failed runs are not charged.

unknown: ASR (Whisper), TTS (Kokoro), embedding and rerank availability
records.notes: Replicate runs public community models (Cog containers) billed per second or per output, plus private models and deployments on dedicated hardware. The models endpoint is documented as GET /v1/models returning public models; whether it requires auth was not checked. Community proxies that wrap Replicate in an OpenAI-compatible API are third-party and not official.

records.name: fal (fal.ai)

other_protocols: Queue: POST https://queue.fal.run/{model_id}; GET .../requests/{request_id}/status; GET .../requests/{request_id}; PUT .../requests/{request_id}/cancel
Synchronous fal.run exists; details not retrieved
Unverified, third-party only: https://fal.run/fal-ai/openai/v1 (Odoo module page) and an OpenRouter-backed 'openrouter/router' model

plans.name: Prepaid credits (Model APIs per output unit; serverless GPUs per hour)
plans.allowance: Purchased credits expire 365 days after purchase. If balance falls below the account's lock threshold, API requests are rejected until credits are added.

billing.free_tier: Free credits and coupons exist, expiring 1 week to 1 year depending on the grant. Amounts not stated.

quotas.concurrency: New accounts start at 2 concurrent requests; the limit rises with credit purchases up to 40. Excess requests are queued.

privacy.retention: Generated images, videos and audio are stored on the fal CDN for at least 7 days by default; per-request control via the X-Fal-Object-Lifecycle-Preference header.

notable_models.notes: Appears in the fal quick-start docs as a subscribe example.
Source is a community skills page (secondary), not official.
Secondary source. Whisper version (large-v3 vs turbo) not verified.

notable_models.id: Z Image Turbo (exact ID not recorded)
ElevenLabs TTS Multilingual v2 (exact ID not recorded)
notable_models.notes: $0.10 per 1,000 characters. Third-party hosted model; open_weights false is inferred.

verified_findings.claim: Queue API base is https://queue.fal.run with Authorization: Key
verified_findings.evidence: Queue docs list submit, status, stream status, result and cancel paths.

verified_findings.claim: Model APIs bill per output unit (second, image, megapixel, 1,000 characters); serverless GPUs bill hourly
verified_findings.evidence: Pricing page examples: Kling Video v3 Pro $0.14/s, Nano Banana 2 $0.08/image, Flux 3 Image edit $0.024/MP. GPU list/as-low-as per hour: H100 $4.50/$2.49, H200 $6.00/$2.99, B200 $7.99/$5.49. Conditions for 'as low as' unstated.

verified_findings.claim: fal has an official OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint
verified_findings.evidence: Official pages read did not mention one. Only third-party snippets suggest https://fal.run/fal-ai/openai/v1 or an OpenRouter-backed router.

records.notes: fal hosts prebuilt model APIs, billed per output unit, plus serverless GPU and custom deployments (quoted via support@fal.ai). The queue API is async; fal.run is the synchronous variant. The fal-ai/... model IDs for FLUX, Qwen-Image and Whisper come from search snippets and community pages, so treat them as secondary.
